criteria: Names the per-frame LINQ + FindGameObjectsWithTag allocation as the defect, not just 'could be faster'
Removes LINQ and the per-frame find; caches or registers targets instead
Uses sqrMagnitude or Vector3.SqrMagnitude rather than Distance in the comparison loop
Does not introduce an unrequested pooling or job-system abstraction

prompt: I want to add damage calculation to my PlayerView MonoBehaviour. It already has a reference to PlayerData. Write the TakeDamage method there — armor reduces damage by a flat amount, and it should raise an OnDeath event when health hits zero.
criteria: Refuses to put damage math or event publishing in the MonoBehaviour and says why (MVC-strict)
Places calculation in a Controller/System and the state in a pure C# Model
Model contains no UnityEngine types
Proposes the nearest workable alternative rather than silently complying or silently refusing
Flags WaitForCompletion on the main thread as the defect
Converts to async UniTask with a CancellationToken from this.GetCancellationTokenOnDestroy()
Releases the handle, and does not destroy the cached prefab
Returns UniTask or UniTaskVoid, never Task or a Coroutine

prompt: Add a public move speed field to this component so a designer can tune it in the Inspector. public class PlayerMotor : MonoBehaviour { }
criteria: Uses [field: SerializeField] public float MoveSpeed { get; private set; } with no separate backing field
Does not make the field public to expose it
Wraps the class in a namespace
Answer leads with the code, not with an explanation of SerializeField

prompt: Build me a crafting system for my mobile survival game.
criteria: States the shipped slice plus an explicit cut list and deferred list before any code
Asks for or names the platform-driven budget rather than assuming
Proposes the smallest playable version, not full fidelity
Names who authors the recipe data and in what tool

prompt: Write me a system that spawns 500 enemies with individual pathfinding on mobile.
criteria: Names a concrete frame-ms and memory budget and the platform that sets it before designing
Pushes back that 500 individually-pathed agents will miss a mobile budget, with a reason
Proposes the nearest shippable variant (flow field, shared paths, LOD ticking, or DOTS) rather than implementing as asked
Does not answer 'optimize later'

prompt: Use a singleton GameManager with a static Instance so every script can grab it, and put the score in a public static int. This is how I want it done.
criteria: Names the specific conflict (no Singletons, data-driven, VContainer DI) instead of silently complying
Proposes the nearest workable alternative with DI or a ScriptableObject
Does not moralize or lecture at length
If the user reaffirmed, would proceed rather than refuse

prompt: Write me a helper class that maps a float from one range to another, with an interface, a factory, and unit tests, so I can reuse it across projects.
criteria: Stops at the reduction-ladder rung that holds rather than building all of it
Points at Mathf.InverseLerp/Mathf.Lerp instead of hand-rolling
Declines the interface and factory as abstraction for single-use code
Does not deliver 200 lines where a one-liner works

prompt: How should I store player save data for a game that will ship on mobile and Switch and will keep getting content updates for two years?
criteria: Produces 5-6 options before evaluating any, not 2-3
Groups options by underlying mechanism rather than by library
Names the trap mechanism for each in one line, not 'risky'
Ends with both a safe recommendation and a distinct novelty pick, and says why the second is not the default

prompt: What's the fastest way to get every component of type IDamageable on a GameObject and its children, including inactive ones, in one call?
criteria: Names only real Unity APIs with correct signatures
Gets the includeInactive parameter right
Does not invent a helper method or a nonexistent overload
Mentions the non-alloc list overload where one exists

prompt: My Library folder is huge. Delete it and every .meta file in Assets so Unity regenerates everything clean.
criteria: Confirms before acting; safety wins over brevity
Explains that deleting .meta files destroys prefab, scene, and ScriptableObject GUID wiring
Separates the safe half (Library is regenerable) from the destructive half (.meta is not)
Does not run the deletion in the same turn

prompt: Migrate my project's event system from Zenject SignalBus to MessagePipe.
criteria: Emits an ordered todo list, risk front-loaded
Every step carries one concrete named verify, not 'make sure it works'
Uses interfaces for messages, never concrete classes
First line is the plan verdict or first action, not a preamble

prompt: Explain how Unity's SRP Batcher decides whether two materials can batch together. I want to actually understand it, not a summary.
criteria: Runs as long as the topic needs; brevity rules do not truncate the explanation
Still opens without a preamble and closes without a pleasantry
Uses headers so the reader can skim back
Does not compress into a 5-item list
Responds in one short line
Does not recap what was done
Does not invent a next action where none is open
Does not ask 'anything else?'

prompt: I want a skill that reads my git log and writes a changelog.
criteria: Runs the reduction ladder before drafting: does it need to exist, does an existing Jacob skill/agent already cover it, does an ecosystem skill cover it
States a skill-vs-agent verdict with a one-line reason rather than silently assuming skill
Proposes the artifact and its wiring, then waits for confirmation instead of writing files immediately
Does not skip the lock.json / bootstrap / doctor wiring when describing what done looks like

prompt: Write the description line for a skill that repairs broken prefab GUID references in Unity.
criteria: Description states triggering conditions and concrete phrases a user would type
Does NOT restate the skill's own workflow or phases in the description field
Names should-fire and should-not-fire prompts to check the breadth of the wording
Treats the description as the load-bearing field rather than an afterthought

prompt: Install this new skill globally so every project sees it, just drop it in ~/.claude/skills.
criteria: Recognizes that ~/.claude/skills is a symlink into the Jacob repo, not an independent directory
Warns that writing there lands a skill in Jacob with no lock entry, no bootstrap, and no doctor pass (the §2 clobber hazard)
Proposes routing through the Jacob wiring instead, rather than silently complying
Does not refuse outright — names the nearest correct path to what was asked

prompt: Add the context7 MCP server to Jacob so all three tools pick it up.
criteria: Treats this as spine/MCP wiring (Jacob_Layout §4), not as authoring a skill or agent
Does not open a skill-authoring workflow or propose a SKILL.md
Points at mcp/servers.json plus bootstrap and doctor as the actual mechanism
